concerns.text: Incremental-value claim is confounded by changing BOTH the feature set and the model class (Random Forest baseline vs XGBoost integrated). A performance delta cannot be attributed to SNPs/MGE features when the learner also changes. Use the same learner for both feature sets, or run both learners on both feature sets (2x2).

Mann-Whitney U tests on SNP/MGE distributions between resistant and sensitive isolates ignore clonal population structure — a well-known failure mode in bacterial genomics (phylogenetic confounding). Constitution VI explicitly requires significance 'independent of phylogenetic structure', but no requirement implements this (e.g. stratified/permutation tests, phylogeny-aware GWAS à la bugwas/pyseer). As written, FR-005 cannot satisfy the constitution.

Spec never states whether models are trained per-species and per-antibiotic or pooled. Pooling E. coli and S. aureus (or multiple antibiotics) into one classifier is a category error — species is a near-perfect confounder for both genotype and phenotype. The scope decision lists per-antibiotic tasks but no FR requires per-species/per-antibiotic model separation.

MGE feature is under-specified: 'genomic distance from each ARG to the nearest transposon insertion site or plasmid origin' — no method is named for identifying transposon insertion sites or plasmid origins in assemblies (which tool/database?). Without this, the feature is not reproducible or well-defined. Also note snp-sites extracts SNPs from an existing alignment; the alignment step itself is unspecified.
US-1's test mentions 'held-out test set' while FR-004/Constitution VII specify 5-fold CV only. Clarify the evaluation protocol (nested CV or a held-out split) so the AUC comparison is well-defined.

'strictly greater than or equal to the baseline model's metrics (demonstrating non-degradation)' is a near-vacuous acceptance criterion — adding features to a flexible learner essentially guarantees >= on training-fold metrics. The scientifically meaningful criterion (SC-001's delta, ideally with a significance test on the delta, e.g. paired CV-fold comparison) should replace this.
